title: The second law
target: Explain the direction of heat transfer and the limits of energy conversion.
criteria: Explain why moving heat from cold to hot needs an additional process.
Distinguish energy conservation from process direction.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A warm container and a cooler block touch with no powered device. Which spontaneous net heat flow is expected initially?
options: Warm container to cooler block.
Toward the lighter object regardless of temperature.
No flow unless temperatures are equal.
Cooler block to warm container.
cpa.guide: Spontaneous net heat transfer is from higher to lower temperature.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two objects reach equal temperature in an isolated setup. What is expected about temperature-driven net heat transfer?
options: All particle motion stops.
It must flow from heavier to lighter.
It is zero at thermal equilibrium.
It grows because temperatures match.
cpa.guide: Equal temperature removes the driving temperature difference for net heat transfer.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A refrigerator moves energy from a cold interior to a warmer room. What additional input supports that process?
options: A destruction of energy in the cold space.
A reversal of every physical law.
Work supplied to the refrigerator.
No input is needed because cold creates heat.
cpa.guide: A refrigerator uses work to move heat against its spontaneous direction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A modeled refrigerator removes 75 J from its cold space and receives 25 J of work per cycle. How much energy is rejected to the room?
cpa.guide: For a full cycle with no net stored-energy change, Q_hot = Q_cold + W = 100 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A proposed unpowered process transfers 10 J from a colder object to a hotter object with no other change. What distinguishes the two laws?
options: It violates the first law solely because heat moves.
The energy amounts balance, but the proposed direction conflicts with the second law.
The second law says energy is never conserved.
Both laws permit it just because energy balances.
cpa.guide: Energy conservation alone does not establish that a process direction is possible.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A heat pump’s energy balance is correct on paper. What additional question tests physical feasibility?
options: Whether temperatures can be ignored in every process.
Whether the heat-flow direction and required work are consistent with the second law.
Whether the symbols are written in a favorite color.
Whether energy is allowed to appear from nothing.
cpa.guide: A consistent balance is necessary but process direction and work requirements also matter.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.
